title: Neon seems to be able to one shot simple 3D Games.
author: W2DGAMES
selftext:
[https://wavedash.com/games/mahjong](https://wavedash.com/games/mahjong)

I fancied a game of Mahjong Solitere, so I made my own with Neon. My prompt was pretty detailed to the point it's created it exactly as I wanted both graphically and game UI etc. 

I've got to say as a strong Opus 5.5 users - Neon cooks for 3D and game programming. It's stupidly fast.

comments.author: PhotonStorm
comments.body:
Have been going deep into Gemini 4 Neon as well - and I definitely agree. Yes, it's crazy fast. It will turn around entire games (from scratch) in often < 15 mins. It's highly capable of coding, as you'd expect. Where it definitely falls flat is with any kind of 'creativity'. You totally need to hold this things hand like a toddler crossing the road.

Even on max thinking the results, when left to its own devices, are very underwhelming. Which is fine I guess, that's the whole point - we're meant to be the ones steering these things, right? But with Fable I can throw any kind of crazy concept at it, and it totally dominates. Neon, on the other hand, does the absolute bare minimum, so it either takes a LOT more detailed spec up front, or a LOT more iterations.

But.. it is REALLY fast and is a solid workhorse, so well worth checking out. I've found a good flow where I'll give it a much more detailed spec, lots of example / concept art, work through a few rounds with it and then pass it to Opus or Fable to finish off that final 20%. It's also crazy hard to drain your usage allowance! So yeah... strong agree, but totally underline that "My prompt was pretty detailed" part - because I'd say that bit is a requirement, not optional - unless you like underwhelming, of course.
